hero.lead: A nation of 36.4 million with farmland across almost half its land, where the EU’s recovery funding for Poland totals €54.72 billion and the IMF projects growth of 3.4% this year.

capital.heading: Growth and recovery, and every household above the line.

record.text: Recovery and resilience allocation: €25.28 billion in grants and €29.44 billion in loans; 77% received by October 2026
New EIB Group financing signed in Poland in 2025, a record; financing for climate and environment projects more than doubled on the year to €5.5 billion
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Ten-year green bond in Swiss francs
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · priced 21 May 2026 · matures 5 June 2036 · 90 bp over mid-swaps · yield 1.6425% · issued at par · 94% bought by investors from Switzerland
register.note: One of three tranches of a CHF 885 million issue, the others of three and seven years
register.text: A ten-year green bond of the Republic of Poland in Swiss francs, sold alongside three- and seven-year bonds. As a green bond its proceeds go to environmental projects, which can carry the energy and water standards; the pricing release does not list the projects.

register.name: Three- and seven-year bonds in Swiss francs
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · priced 21 May 2026 · CHF 485M maturing 5 June 2029, 50 bp over mid-swaps, yield 0.8350% · CHF 160M maturing 3 June 2033, 80 bp over mid-swaps, yield 1.3822% · issued at par
register.note: Bought mainly by investors from Switzerland: 80% of the three-year and 83% of the seven-year bond
register.text: Two fixed-rate bonds of the Republic of Poland in Swiss francs, bought mainly by investors from Switzerland. Their proceeds fund the state budget as a whole, which carries the public services behind the seven standards; they are not earmarked to any one standard.

register.name: Seven- and twelve-year euro bonds, with a green tranche
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · priced 30 June 2025 · €1.75bn due 7 July 2032, coupon 3.125%, yield 3.178% · €1.25bn due 7 July 2037, coupon 3.875%, yield 3.903% · demand above €5.7bn · EMTN Programme
register.note: The first green bond issue of Poland since 2019; the Ministry notes that Poland was the first country to issue green bonds, in 2016
register.text: Two euro benchmark bonds of the Republic of Poland, one of them a green bond tranche under the Green Bond Framework, with a second-party opinion from Sustainalytics. The funds of the green tranche finance pro-environmental projects, which can carry the energy and water standards; the release does not say which tranche is green, and the other funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one standard.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · €25.28bn in grants and €29.44bn in loans · fifth payment request assessed positively 10 August 2026 · €7.9bn paid 1 October 2026 · 77% of the allocation received
register.text: EU Recovery and Resilience Facility funding for Poland’s reforms and investments, €25.28 billion in grants and €29.44 billion in loans, with 77% received by October 2026. It finances renewables, power grids and energy-efficient building renovation, laptops and tablets for schools, childcare facilities and hospital modernisation, serving the energy, shelter, education and health standards.
register.note: Key investments include renewables, power grids, energy-efficient building renovation, childcare facilities and hospital modernisation

register.name: Social and affordable rental housing, BGK (second framework loan)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · framework loan to Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego · approved 7 August 2026 · total cost PLN 4,444M (€1,034M) · government rental housing programme
register.note: About 8,750 social and affordable rental homes to be built or refurbished; EIB finance of about €465M
register.text: An EIB framework loan through BGK, Poland’s state development bank, for the construction and refurbishment of about 8,750 social and affordable rental homes under the government rental housing programme. It serves the shelter standard for citizens whose incomes are too low to rent at market rates.

register.name: Energy savings in public buildings and district heating (ELENA)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · EIB Advisory, ELENA · announced 3 March 2026 · National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management (NFOŚiGW) · energy renovation of over 80 public buildings and at least 65 district heating systems
register.note: Annual energy savings of around 23 GWh projected; the ELENA grant amount is not disclosed
register.text: EIB Advisory support under ELENA to prepare almost €300 million of investment by Poland’s environmental fund with national and local authorities. It finances the energy renovation of public buildings and the transformation of district heating systems, serving the energy standard.

register.name: Agriculture and rural development, Ministry of Finance
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signature with the Polish Ministry of Finance announced, as reported in the EIB release of 19 February 2026 · part of €1.3bn in new financing approved by the EIB
register.note: For small entrepreneurs and individual farmers: digitalisation, energy efficiency, afforestation, soil protection and animal welfare in food production
register.text: An EIB financing agreement with the Republic of Poland, part of €1.3 billion approved to support the development of Polish agriculture and rural areas. It reaches small entrepreneurs and individual farmers who produce the nation’s food, serving the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Aid Fund for Ukrainian citizens under temporary protection
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · additional loan approved 13 June 2025 · raises the CEB loan from €565M to €740M · earlier additional €115M approved 7 June 2024 under the Public Sector Finance Facility
register.note: The initial loan of €450 million, approved in June 2022, was the largest in the CEB’s history at the time
register.text: A CEB loan to the Republic of Poland for the Aid Fund for Ukrainian citizens under temporary protection, for vulnerable arrivals such as single parents, older people and families with children. It sustains social and family allowances and basic access to essential services, serving the livelihood standard, the standard furthest from reach in Poland.

register.name: Miejska Górka onshore wind farm, TAURON
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 29 July 2026 · PLN 1.12bn · 190 MW in the Greater Poland region · operation planned for 2027 · EIB provides over half of the project’s total cost
register.note: Poland’s second-largest onshore wind farm, to supply nearly 200,000 households
register.text: An EIB loan of over €260 million to the power utility TAURON for a 190 MW onshore wind farm in western Poland. It adds clean power for nearly 200,000 households and serves the energy standard.

register.name: BC-Wind offshore wind farm, Ocean Winds
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 28 November 2025 · 390 MW from 26 turbines of up to 15 MW · part of a financing of around €2bn with 15 lenders
register.note: The EIB is the largest lender; the farm is to supply nearly half a million Polish households and businesses
register.text: An EIB loan to the BC-Wind offshore wind farm, developed by Ocean Winds, a joint venture of ENGIE and EDPR. It brings clean power to nearly half a million Polish households and businesses and serves the energy standard.

register.name: Loans for micro, small and medium enterprises, EFL (Crédit Agricole)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 20 November 2025 · loan to Crédit Agricole SA for its Polish leasing company Europejski Fundusz Leasingowy · about 30% for businesses owned or led by women
register.note: Expected to reach about 12,500 Polish micro, small and medium enterprises, including in struggling regions
register.text: A CEB loan channelled through Europejski Fundusz Leasingowy to micro, small and medium enterprises in Poland, with easier access to finance for disadvantaged groups and businesses in struggling regions. It serves the livelihood standard, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Energy-efficiency loans for housing associations, BNP Paribas Bank Polska
register.detail: European Investment Fund · InvestEU portfolio guarantee of up to €105M · signed 26 November 2024 · over €160M of new debt financing, of which €40M for housing associations
register.note: A further €40 million for micro and small companies investing in energy efficiency and renewable energy
register.text: An EIF guarantee under InvestEU that lets BNP Paribas Bank Polska lend over €160 million, with €40 million earmarked for housing associations modernising residential buildings for better energy efficiency. It serves the shelter and energy standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.5% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: Spółdzielnia Socjalna „Integracja”
items.text: A social cooperative in Adelin, founded in 2020 by the Gmina of Zabrodzie and the Wyszków district, that provides catering to various local bodies and now delivers balanced, easily digestible meals adapted to low-sodium, diabetic and gluten-free diets to the homes of older people.

items.name: Habitat for Humanity Poland
items.text: A housing foundation, part-funded by its ReStore charity furniture shop, that in 2025 helped 117 households, almost 400 people, into homes on the private rental market and supported a social rental agency model in Dąbrowa Górnicza.

items.name: Spółdzielnia Socjalna „Rodzinny Dom”
items.text: A social cooperative in Długi Kąt that since 2018, on commission from the town of Józefów na Roztoczu, has run a round-the-clock home for eight dependent older people, with six staff on employment contracts, at a monthly cost well below that of a traditional social care home.

items.name: Spółdzielnia Socjalna „Podkowa”
items.text: A social cooperative created in 2021 by the town of Kobyłka and the Gmina of Jadów that provides care, personal assistance and respite services in Kobyłka and neighbouring municipalities, and cleaning and maintenance services in Jadów, employing about 50 people.

items.name: Spółdzielnia Socjalna „Odmiana”
items.text: A social cooperative created by the Krokus Wiązowna Foundation and the Gmina of Wiązowna to give work to people at risk of exclusion, which in 2024 provided care services to 29 people and handyman services to 40 on commission from the local Centre for Social Services.

items.name: Spółdzielnia Socjalna DALBA
items.text: A social cooperative that runs a craft brewery in Puck and a pub in Gdańsk, teaches brewing, numeracy, literacy and organisational skills, and employs mostly people who had no chance on the open labour market because of their disability.

items.name: Arte Cooperative
items.text: A cooperative in Bielawa that helps people facing homelessness or addiction learn new skills and enter the labour market, featured by the European Social Fund Plus in April 2026.
